title: Partner marketplace mini-heuristics & asset matrix (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, pragmatic checklist + small copy bank to accelerate marketplace + partner co-sell listings. It is intentionally lightweight — meant for partner PMs, partner ops, and GTM copy owners to iterate quickly before filling formal listing templates for AWS/Azure/GCP and private reseller portals.

Status: draft, rough wording, contains heuristics rather than strict gating rules. Use as a preflight to reduce time in publisher QA.

Quick heuristics (why these items matter):
- Single-sentence value prop first: customers scan tiles quickly; the first line must answer "what problem does this solve for my product team?"
- Use buyer-focused verbs (reduce, speed, control) not platform jargon (inference runtime, KV cache).
- Three levels of copy: tile (6–10 words), short description (20–40 words), long description (60–110 words). Keep consistent voice across levels.
- Technical bullets are for engineers; benefits bullets are for product leads/POs. Always include at least 1 benefit bullet.
- Localization note: for APAC marketplace copies, avoid culturally specific idioms; prefer simple structure and local currency examples (if present).

Asset matrix (minimal required + recommended):
- Tile title (required) -> 6–10 words, include "Redwood Inference" only where publisher guidelines ask for vendor name.
- Tile tagline (required) -> 6–12 words, benefit-forward.
- Short description (required) -> 20–40 words, 1–2 sentences.
- Long description (required) -> 60–110 words, up to 3 short paragraphs. Include use cases and supported deployment modes.
- 3–5 feature bullets (required) -> mix of product features and outcomes (e.g., "Reduce per-token inference cost with automatic batching").
- 2–3 technical bullets (recommended) -> model families supported, latency SLOs, GPU types, compatibility notes.
- Supported regions / cloud regions statement (required) -> e.g., "Available in us-west1, eu-west1; contact sales for private/on-prem options."
- Pricing summary (required) -> short: hosted (usage-based), dedicated (commit), private (license + support). Avoid specific $ amounts unless publisher requires them.
- Trial CTA and trial duration (recommended) -> what qualifies, e.g., "14-day sandbox" or "credits for evaluation".
- Product screenshots (recommended) -> 2 images: Console route + ROI dashboard or latency/cost chart. JPG or PNG.
- Architecture diagram (recommended) -> PNG + alt text. Emphasize routing, model catalog, and private/VPC option.
- Terms & SLA link (required) -> link to hosted SLA doc, support tiers, data residency info.
- Compliance badges (optional) -> SOC2, ISO27001, FedRAMP (if applicable). Provide pdf artifacts in publisher bundle.
- Logos and vendor asset pack (required) -> high-res PNG, circle and horizontal variants, brand color hex.
- Contact & sales routing (required) -> publisher-specific contact email plus Redwood inbound link.
- SKU mapping (required for metered marketplaces) -> internal SKU ids + metric unit (tokens, embedding units).

Marketplace-specific notes (common cross-publishers):
- AWS: they want short bullets to match "what it does", "how to get started" and a curated screenshot of the console. Provide CloudFormation/Quick Start snippet if we support it.
- Azure: emphasize enterprise integrations (AAD, private links), and include tenant-onboarding steps.
- GCP: prefer explicit region availability + billing mapping; include sample gcloud CLI snippet if applicable.
- Partner co-sell: include joint customer references and co-marketing credit language if partner requests it. Draft a 1–2 sentence partner summary for partner approval.

Copy bank (quick candidates — edit for tone and publisher length limits):
- Tile tagline (6–10 words): "High-performance LLM inference, predictable costs."
- Short (30 words): "Redwood Inference delivers production-grade LLM serving with low latency, cost controls, and private deployment options. Ship reliable generative features across hosted, dedicated, and VPC environments."
- Long (80 words): "Redwood Inference provides a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model inference. Leverage hosted APIs for fast onboarding, reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or a Private VPC/on‑prem installation for regulated workloads. Built-in routing, batching, and quantization suggestions reduce per-token costs while observability and rollout controls protect application quality. Ideal for product teams building chat, search, and embedding features who need latency and cost predictability at scale."
- 3 Benefit bullets (short):
  • "Predictable latency and unit economics for production applications."
  • "Seamless upgrade and model rollouts with canary and fallback policies."
  • "Enterprise-ready: VPC, KMS integration, and audit logs for compliance."
- 2 Technical bullets (short):
  • "Supports leading open models and optimized kernels for GPU inference."
  • "AutoscalingDedicated pools and configurable burst capacity for throughput spikes."

Placeholder snippets for deployment options (one-line each):
- Hosted API: "Self-serve REST/SDK with streaming, function-calling, and transparent performance profiles."
- Dedicated: "Reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and SLAs (monthly/annual commits)."
- Private: "Customer-controlled VPC or on‑prem package with KMS/HSM integrations and audit trails."

Acceptance gates (pre-publish checklist) — must be ticked before sending to publisher QA: 
- [ ] Title + tagline finalized and under 120 characters combined (publisher limits vary).
- [ ] Short + long descriptions reviewed by legal for claims and compliance.
- [ ] Pricing summary aligned with finance (no hard $ unless approved).
- [ ] SKU mapping validated with billing team and mock invoice example attached.
- [ ] Screenshots and diagrams uploaded with alt text.
- [ ] Trial terms or free credits documented and have a clear eligibility flow.
- [ ] Compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO) attached or referenced.
- [ ] Contact routing: partner contact + Redwood sales alias verified.
- [ ] Translation/localization owner assigned for APAC/EU markets.

Operational runbook (publisher queries we commonly get) — suggested answers: 
- Q: "How do customers evaluate?"
  A: "Provide a 14-day sandbox credit and a quickstart found at: https://redwood.ai/quickstart (link to be replaced with publisher-accepted URL)."
- Q: "What support SLAs exist for trials?"
  A: "Standard trial support via docs + email; paid tiers include 24x7 support and elevated response SLAs."
- Q: "How is billing handled?"
  A: "For hosted listings: usage-based billing through publisher marketplace. For Dedicated/Private: contact Redwood sales for committed pricing and invoicing."

Localization and APAC adjustments (practical tips):
- Provide clean, short sentences; avoid idioms.
- Currency: use publisher locale mapping rather than hard-coded amounts.
- Include "data residency" line early if customer needs APAC-region guarantees.
- Translate only final copy; leave templated CTAs untranslated until legal approves.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether we should include model family names in public copy or keep them in technical bullets only (ask Product).
- Obtain finalized trial credit amount and eligibility flow from finance (JIRA-GTM-782).
- Get legal signoff on the "predictable latency" claim for marketing copy.
- Compile SOC2 attestation PDF and attach to publisher bundle.

Next steps and owners (short):
- Assign copy owner to finalize short + long descriptions: Priya Rao (due 2025-03-05).
- SKU mapping + billing example: Liam O'Connor (due 2025-03-07).
- Screenshots + diagrams: Diego Martinez (due 2025-03-05).
- Legal + compliance attachments: Asha Verma to coordinate with Legal (due 2025-03-10).

Slack/refs: see thread #partner-marketplace for back-and-forth and the linked Confluence (CONFLUENCE-12345).

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep this doc short; use it as a preflight to the publisher checklist.
- When publisher templates arrive, map fields from this matrix to their schema (tile -> short_name, long_desc -> detailed_description, etc.).

End.
